units.name: Introduction
units.assessment: Can you trace the classical, lectin and alternative pathways to the terminal C5b-9 complex, and name the regulatory proteins whose loss or inhibition produces complement-mediated hemolysis or microangiopathy?

lesson.title: Archive: The Role of Complement in Kidney Disease
lesson.why: A full academic session on complement biology and how dysregulation causes disease, which is the mechanistic foundation the rest of this chapter builds on.

units.name: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
units.assessment: Can you explain how a somatic PIGA mutation strips CD55 and CD59 from the cell surface, and how flow cytometry with FLAER quantifies the PNH clone in granulocytes, monocytes and red cells?

lesson.title: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria: A Review and an Appraisal of a Changing Treatment Landscape
lesson.why: An academic review of PNH that covers the biology, the flow cytometric definition of the clone, and how the treatment landscape has changed beyond C5 inhibition.

drills.name: Pathophysiology and diagnosis
drills.title: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) Pathophysiology, Symptoms, and Diagnosis

units.name: Clinical manifestations
units.assessment: Can you account for the combination of intravascular hemolysis, thrombosis and marrow failure in PNH, and explain why thrombosis strikes unusual sites such as the hepatic and cerebral veins?

lesson.title: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria & Aplastic Anemia - Monika Oliver BSc MD FRCPC
lesson.channel: The Aplastic Anemia & Myelodysplasia Association of Canada (AAMAC)
lesson.why: Presents PNH together with aplastic anemia, which is how the clinical syndrome actually appears - hemolysis, thrombosis and an underlying failing marrow.

units.name: Treatment
units.assessment: Can you explain why C5 inhibition unmasks C3d-mediated extravascular hemolysis, what proximal inhibitors such as pegcetacoplan and iptacopan add, and what vaccination and antibiotic cover are required before starting?

lesson.title: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria | Oncology Today with Dr Neil Love: Management of Paroxysmal ...
lesson.why: A recent clinician-to-clinician discussion of how PNH is managed now that proximal complement inhibitors sit alongside eculizumab and ravulizumab.

drills.name: Changing treatment landscape
drills.title: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria: A Review and an Appraisal of a Changing Treatment Landscape

units.name: Prognosis
units.assessment: Can you state what now determines long-term survival in PNH on complement inhibition, how breakthrough hemolysis is recognised and worked up, and which patients should still be referred for allogeneic transplant?

lesson.note: Re-searched on the prognostic questions themselves - survival on complement inhibition, breakthrough hemolysis, extravascular hemolysis on C5 blockade, and transplant indications in PNH. The search returned a single candidate, and it is about inebilizumab in neuromyelitis optica, an unrelated disease. Nothing usable exists in the pool for this section.

units.name: Thrombotic microangiopathies
units.assessment: Can you list the entities that present with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia, and outline the first-pass tests that separate TTP, Shiga toxin HUS, complement-mediated HUS and secondary TMA?

lesson.title: Rational Approach to Evaluation of Thrombotic Microangiopathy
lesson.why: A rational, test-by-test approach to the patient with a microangiopathy, which is exactly the triage this section is asking you to be able to perform.

units.assessment: Can you describe the organ involvement that distinguishes complement-mediated TMA from TTP at presentation, and the features that should make you suspect a drug-associated, pregnancy-associated or transplant-associated cause?

units.name: Pathogenesis
units.assessment: Can you explain how ADAMTS13 deficiency generates platelet-rich microthrombi under high shear, and how loss-of-function variants in factor H, factor I or MCP allow uncontrolled alternative pathway activation in aHUS?
